data.title: Verisk to Proceed With $2.35B AccuLynx Deal Following Court Order
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Verisk will proceed with its $2.35 billion acquisition of AccuLynx following a Delaware Supreme Court order.

The state's high court on Friday affirmed a Delaware Chancery Court ruling that found the data analytics and technology provider wasn't allowed to terminate its acquisition of AccuLynx.

Verisk in August had said it strongly disagreed with that decision.

Verisk in the summer of 2025 agreed to buy AccuLynx, a cloud-based project management tool for roofing contractors, for $2.35 billion. Verisk cancelled the deal in December, stating that the Federal Trade commission didn't complete its transaction review by the Dec. 26 deadline.

The Delaware Chancery in August ruled in favor of AccuLynx, and said that the termination was invalid.

Write to Natalie Weger at natalie.weger@wsj.com.

data.title: CVC, GBL hold 74.3% of Italian drugmaker Recordati at end of takeover offer period
data.description:
CVC and Belgian investment firm GBL , which this month raised their bid for Italian pharmaceutical group Recordati to €53 a share, had secured a 74.3% stake in the firm by the end of the offer period, a regulatory filing showed on Friday.

  • That put the consortium above the 66.7% minimum acceptance threshold they had set for the offer — which values Recordati at around €11 billion — but short of the 90% level required to delist the drugmaker

  • The Italian Stock Exchange said on Friday investors had tendered Recordati shares to the bidding consortium for a 62.15% stake

  • That adds to a further 6.9% stake acquired by CVC on the market, GBL's 3.3% holding and an additional 1.96% stake obtained by CVC through the exercise of derivatives

  • The bidders will reopen the offer between November 3 and 9

  • Their vehicle has said that, should the 90% threshold not be reached, it could pursue a merger with Recordati, leaving minority shareholders with stock in an unlisted company

  • Recordati owns treasury shares for around 0.5% of its capital, according to a financial source

data.title: US CDC says measles cases rise to 4,588 as outbreak continues
data.description:
The US CDC on Friday reported 4,588 measles cases in the country as of October 22, up 178 from a week earlier, as an outbreak of the highly contagious disease continues.

Here are some key details:

  • Measles-related hospitalizations this year stand at 479, according to CDC

  • The Pennsylvania state health department has reported five measles-related deaths so far in 2026, but the CDC has confirmed only three measles-associated deaths

  • Pennsylvania reported 1,338 measles cases so far as of October 23, with 255 hospitalizations, according to state health department data

  • Children and teenagers aged 5 to 19 constituted the largest group of people affected by the disease at 1,914, or 42% of all reported cases, followed by adults aged 20 and older at 1,881 cases or 41%, CDC data showed

  • The CDC previously said it would deploy additional support to Pennsylvania to help investigate the outbreak

data.title: Genentech Presents Interim Phase III Data Showing Sefaxersen Significantly Reduced Proteinuria in People With IgA Nephropathy (IgAN)
data.description:
Genentech, a member of the Roche Group (, ROP; ), announced today late-breaking oral presentation data from the ongoing Phase III IMAgINATION study in adults with primary IgA nephropathy (IgAN) receiving optimized standard of care, demonstrating that investigational sefaxersen achieved a statistically significant and clinically meaningful 43.1% reduction in proteinuria (95% confidence interval [CI]: 32.5 - 52.0, P<0.0001), relative to placebo at 37 weeks, as measured by 24-hour urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR). Proteinuria is a key indicator of kidney damage and a reduction in UPCR is strongly associated with the preservation of long-term kidney function. Results presented at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 also showed that, among patients with baseline hematuria (blood in urine), a greater proportion of patients achieved hematuria resolution at Week 37 with sefaxersen versus placebo.

“These Phase III results demonstrate the potential for sefaxersen to meaningfully reduce protein in the urine, a key indicator of kidney damage, in people with IgA nephropathy,” said Levi Garraway, M.D., Ph.D., chief medical officer and head of Global Product Development. “By inhibiting complement factor B in the liver, sefaxersen may offer a novel approach to slow disease progression in IgAN, potentially helping patients delay or avoid long-term dialysis or kidney transplantation.”

The treatment effect in all prespecified subgroups was consistent with the clinically meaningful reductions in proteinuria shown in the primary endpoint results. Sefaxersen was well tolerated with a safety profile consistent with the previously reported Phase II study, exhibiting no new safety signals.

Sefaxersen is an investigational once-monthly subcutaneous injection designed to enable convenient self-administration for people with IgAN. The IMAgINATION study will continue as a blinded study to evaluate the change in kidney function over two years, as measured by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 105. Data will be shared with health authorities, with the goal of bringing this treatment to patients as soon as possible.

Typically diagnosed before the age of 40, IgAN affects at least 25 adults per million worldwide each year. IgAN, also known as Berger’s disease, is a chronic and progressive autoimmune disease that leads to end-stage kidney disease in up to 50% of patients within 20 years of diagnosis. It is the most common form of primary glomerulonephritis (inflammation of the tiny filters, glomeruli, in the kidneys) and is a major cause of chronic kidney disease as well as kidney failure.

About sefaxersen

Investigational sefaxersen is the first highly specific liver-directed antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) inhibitor of factor B production being evaluated in IgA nephropathy (IgAN). Serum complement factor B levels are elevated in people with IgAN. When we reduce these levels, it in turn reduces the level of protein in urine, which is a key indicator of improved kidney function.

Sefaxersen is designed to provide sustained control of the alternative complement pathway, an important pathway in IgAN, enabling once-monthly subcutaneous dosing and is intended for self-administration in people with IgAN. In Phase I and II trials, sefaxersen was shown to be generally well tolerated in healthy volunteers and people with IgAN who were at high risk of progression, and reduced proteinuria and plasma complement factor B.

Roche licensed sefaxersen from Ionis Pharmaceuticals for the treatment of complement mediated diseases.

About the IMAgINATION Study

IMAgINATION [NCT05797610] is a Phase III, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous sefaxersen, an investigational antisense inhibitor of complement factor B, in patients with primary IgA nephropathy at high risk of progression. The study enrolled 459 people, who are randomized 1:1 to receive sefaxersen or placebo for 105 weeks. Participants may switch to open-label treatment after week 105 at the investigator’s discretion or after the common-close timepoint, whichever occurs first. The primary endpoint of the study is the change from baseline in the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio at 37 weeks.

About primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN)

IgAN, also known as Berger’s disease, is a serious, chronic and progressive autoimmune kidney disease affecting at least 25 adults per million worldwide each year and is typically diagnosed before the age of 40 years. In IgAN, immune complexes deposit in the kidneys, which activates the complement system’s alternative pathway, leading to inflammation and subsequent kidney damage. It is the most common form of primary glomerulonephritis (inflammation of kidney glomeruli) and remains a leading cause of kidney failure, with up to 50% of patients experiencing end-stage kidney disease within 20 years of diagnosis. Many current therapies aim to reduce protein levels in the urine and control blood pressure to slow progression of the disease.

Updated KDIGO 2025 guidelines* highlight the need to address both the underlying immune-mediated causes of IgAN and the downstream consequences of kidney damage. While new therapies have expanded treatment options, important unmet needs remain, including improved long-term preservation of kidney function and more targeted approaches that address key drivers of disease progression.

About Genentech in Immunology

Genentech is committed to harnessing pioneering science and innovation to address critical unmet needs for patients with immune-mediated diseases. Our pipeline includes over a dozen clinical programs in immunology aiming to transform care for people living with lupus, MASH, ulcerative colitis, Crohn’s disease, immunoglobulin A nephropathy, idiopathic nephrotic syndrome, and rheumatoid arthritis. We are investing end-to-end in immunology from discovery to R&D to commercialization across a variety of modalities including monoclonal antibodies, bispecifics, and CAR-T cell therapies to help solve some of the most difficult challenges in immunology today.

About Genentech

Founded 50 years ago, Genentech is a leading biotechnology company that discovers, develops, manufactures and commercializes medicines to treat patients with serious and life-threatening medical conditions. The company, a member of the Roche Group, has headquarters in South San Francisco, California. For additional information about the company, please visit http://www.gene.com.

*KDIGO guidelines serve as the foundational framework for healthcare organizations, policymakers, and clinicians worldwide to standardize kidney disease diagnosis, staging, and treatment.

data.title: Lockheed Martin’s Growth Potential ‘Not Priced Into The Stock,’ UBS Says — Analyst Sees About 15% Upside Potential In LMT Shares
data.description:
Key points:
  • RBC Capital raised its price target on Lockheed Martin to $600 from $550 while maintaining a ‘Sector Perform’ rating, citing strong bookings and encouraging initial commentary on 2027.
  • Barclays also raised its Price Target to $560 from $554 and maintained an ‘Equal Weight’ rating.
  • According to Koyfin data, 12 of the 23 analysts covering LMT rate it ‘Hold’, while 10 have a ‘Buy’ or ‘Strong Buy’ rating.

Lockheed Martin (LMT) shares were in focus on Friday after multiple analysts raised their price targets on the stock following better-than-expected Q3 results and increased full year 2026 outlook.

According to The Fly, UBS said Lockheed Martin’s long-term growth narrative is not priced into the stock, while RBC cited very strong bookings and encouraging initial commentary on FY2027 as it raised its price target to $600 from $550 and kept a ‘Sector Perform’ rating.

LMT shares traded 2% high at the time of writing.

According to Koyfin data, 12 out of 23 analysts covering the stock rate it ‘Hold’ whereas 10 rate it ‘Buy’ or ‘Strong Buy’.

Analysts Raise Price Targets On LMT

UBS raised its price target on Lockheed Martin to $692 from $653 and maintained a ‘Buy’ rating. The firm also noted that Lockheed’s growth had accelerated for two consecutive quarters, reaching 11% in the latest quarter.

Citi analyst John Godyn raised his price target to $706 from $691 and maintained a ‘Buy’ rating, according to The Fly. The firm cited increased confidence in accelerating momentum across Lockheed Martin’s segments.

Barclays analyst Anthony Valentini raised his target to $560 from $554 and maintained an ‘Equal Weight’ rating.

Q3 Earnings Highlights

Lockheed Martin reported third-quarter revenue of $20.71 billion, up 11% year over year and above the analyst estimate of $20.46 billion, while diluted earnings-per-share (EPS) rose to $7.97 from $6.95, beating the $7.52 estimate, according to estimates compiled by Fiscal AI.

The company also raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $80 billion–$82 billion and EPS forecast to $30.35–$30.75, marking its second consecutive quarterly guidance increase.

Lockheed Martin’s backlog reached a record $292 billion, up 27% from the previous quarter, with a book-to-bill ratio of 4x, meaning orders significantly exceeded sales during the quarter.

The company raised its full-year free cash flow outlook to $7.8 billion–$8.0 billion, up from its previous forecast of $7.0 billion–$7.2 billion.

F-35 Framework Still Awaits Formal Contract

Separately on Thursday, Lockheed Martin and the Department of War announced a 10-year framework covering 850 U.S. F-35 aircraft, associated initial spare parts, 10 years of modification kits and sustainment, as well as international customer orders across Lots 21–30. Production is planned to continue at 156 aircraft annually across U.S. and international customers.

The framework is not yet a finalized contract. A formal award is subject to multiyear contracting authority and associated appropriations, after which Lockheed Martin and the F-35 Joint Program Office can finalize contract terms, pricing and schedules. Lockheed Martin said the proposed arrangement is intended to improve production planning and supply-chain stability, with expected savings from long-term pricing and volume discounts.

How Retail Views LMT

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment remained in the ‘bullish’ territory amid ‘high’ message volumes in the past 24 hours.

LMT shares have gained over 23% year-to-date.

data.title: Dr Reddy’s on track to restart semaglutide rollout; Canada to drive initial demand
data.description:
Dr Reddy’s Laboratories expects to resume semaglutide supplies across key international markets from November after resolving manufacturing issues that disrupted the product's rollout earlier this year. Canada is likely to account for the bulk of initial sales volumes.

During a call with journalists, the company's management said it had resolved issues related to semaglutide active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) production and was proceeding with formulation batches ahead of the relaunch.

Management said the company was “on track to resolve issues associated with the semaglutide API” and, based on current progress, the relaunch was most likely in November.

“We will launch in November and the numbers for both Q3 and Q4 will be 6 to 7 million units across 10 markets,” CEO Erez Israeli said, adding that Canada would account for the majority of those volumes.

The company clarified that no fresh regulatory approval was required in Canada.

“We voluntarily, when we had the scale-up issue, decided not to continue the marketing of the product. We solved our scale-up issue of the API and we are back to the market after we solved the problem,” Israeli added.

The company had previously made a provision of Rs 240 crore in the June quarter for inventory and other costs related to the semaglutide API issue. While the charge weighed on first-quarter profitability, Dr Reddy’s said it did not expect similar financial hits going forward.

“Based on the current way in which we are tracking all the activities, we don't expect such type of P&L hits going forward,” CFO M.V. Narasimham said.

The Hyderabad-based drugmaker already has approvals for semaglutide in 10 countries, including India and Canada, while eight approvals have come from emerging markets across Latin America, Africa and the Middle East.

Management said Canada would remain the centrepiece of the near-term opportunity. The company expects to supply the product in the current quarter and begin meeting demand that accumulated during the temporary withdrawal.

Dr Reddy’s remains optimistic that the temporary disruption has not materially affected the market opportunity.

“The opportunity is very much there. The market was underserved. There was not enough generic product in the market,” management said. Israeli noted that discussions with customers in Canada were continuing and that the company expected a “very successful launch”.

Beyond Canada, the company is preparing to launch the product in additional international markets. Management highlighted recent approvals, including in Chile, where Dr Reddy’s is the first generic entrant, and said more emerging markets were expected to open up over the next few years.

“We got approval in Chile and we are the first generic in that market. As we move along in the later years, you will have the launch of this product in Europe as well as in the US,” Israeli added.

In India, Dr Reddy’s said it had maintained its market presence through an alternative supply arrangement after the manufacturing issue emerged. The company continues to market semaglutide products for both diabetes and weight management indications and plans to maintain its full product range.

For Dr Reddy’s, semaglutide is emerging as a key global growth driver, with management indicating that demand remains strong and that the planned relaunch marks the beginning of a broader, multi-year opportunity.

data.title: US energy firms kept rig count unchanged for second week in a row, Baker Hughes says
data.description:
US energy firms this week kept the total rig count unchanged for a second week in a row, energy services firm Baker Hughes said in its closely followed report on Friday.

The total oil and gas rig count, an early indicator of future output, held steady at 603 during the week ended October 23. (BHGUSWTT), (BHGUSOILDRLW), (BHGUSGASDRLW) (USOIRC=ECI), (USGSRC=ECI)

Baker Hughes said the total rig count was up 53 rigs, or 10% above this time last year.

Baker Hughes said oil rigs rose by one to 460 this week, the highest since early October, while gas rigs fell by one to 132, the lowest since early October. Other miscellaneous rigs held at 11.

The oil and gas rig count declined by 7% in 2025, 5% in 2024, and 20% in 2023 as lower US oil prices prompted energy firms to focus more on boosting shareholder returns and paying down debt rather than increasing output.

But US producers got an incentive to drill as oil prices spiked with the US-Israeli war on Iran, putting spot US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude prices on track for the first annual rise in four years. The US Energy Information Administration (EIA) projected that crude output will rise from a record 13.7 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2025 to 13.9 million bpd in 2026.

On the gas side, EIA projected output will jump from a record 107.6 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) in 2025 to 112.2 bcfd in 2026 as demand for the fuel rises to produce electricity for power-hungry data centers and liquefied natural gas (LNG) for export.

data.title: Oil Freight Rates Surge Over $20/bbl From Year Ago, Goldman Says — OPIS
data.description:
The average global crude-oil freight rate has recently surged to more than $20/bbl higher than the level during the same time last year, a move that could reduce refiners' overall demand for crude or skew it toward more closely located suppliers, Goldman Sachs energy analysts said.

The investment bank said the rally in crude freight rates initially began in the very large crude carrier segment and on Middle Eastern routes, but it has since spread to all major crude trading routes, particularly affecting long-haul voyages around the world.

Goldman said there are five drivers behind the $20/bbl year-on-year increase in the average global shipping freight rate, which is calculated based on its 14-day moving average.

They are: Strait of Hormuz crossing risk premium ($7); Ship-to-ship transfers outside of the Persian Gulf that tie up tankers for longer ($4); higher maritime bunker fuel prices ($4); inefficient tanker allocation and increased tanker redirections ($3); and the blockage of the Iranian fleet that boosts demand for non-sanctioned tankers ($2).

The bank said crude producers that rely heavily on distant buyers may have to discount their supplies more heavily to retain demand from refiners facing high transportation costs. They include Middle East producers that sell oil to refiners in Asia and U.S. producers of West Texas Intermediate crude sold to Europe or East Asia.

On the other hand, prices of crude from more centrally located producers may gain from some demand reallocation, like those producers that are selling Brent crudes in northwestern Europe or ESPO in Russia, Goldman said.

Meanwhile, refiners that reply on imported crude from distant suppliers such as Asian refiners would have to either pass higher freight costs onto final consumers or accept lower net refinery margins, the bank said.

Goldman said high freight costs have weighed particularly heavily on Asian refineries' net margins, as oil demand in countries like China is more flexible because of alternative fuels such as electrons for EVs, threatening Asian fuel production and potentially raising global refined product prices.

"Overall, we see high freight rates widening crude price differentials by changing crude trading patterns and supporting refined product prices, while suppressing refiners' net margins," the bank said.

On Thursday, Valero Energy's vice president of crude, feedstocks supply and trading, Randy Hawkins, said in an analyst call that a sharp increase in freight rates since the start of the Iran war has forced some refiners to scramble for nearby crude feedstock supply, with some oil producers discounting their supplies to account for the higher freight cost.

The cost to move a very large crude carrier, which typically carries 2 million bbl from the U.S. Gulf Coast to Asia, is now around $30-35/bbl, up from a 2025 average of around $5/bbl, he said.
